system.description:
Many people in the Empire have no formal education. They rely on a mixture of common sense, folklore, tradition and practical skills borne out of hard experience.

Empire folk are, by and large, insular and gossipy, but to charm and gullible, however, an individual with a practiced peddler's patter and a charming manner can often pass for a respected expert or trustworthy authority when they are really just a swindler.

There are numerous ways in which these con artists fool credulous folk into believing them. Some pretend to be merchants who require a bit of cash in order to invest in a sure fire business venture that will make everyone involved stinking rich. Others play the part of seers, divining the future in the turn of a card or a vial of potion glimpsed in a crystal ball. Some pretend to be priests, selling salvation or displays of faith healing. Among their most notorious schemes is when charlatans pose as physicians who provide miraculous cures for a handful of illnesses.

The proffered concoctions are normally little more than coloured water, perhaps spiked with stimulants in order to provide an immediate, but short-lived, feeling of improved hard experience.
system.summary: An unscrupulous con artist, with charm, discipline, and a knack for persuasion, the Charlatan is a master of deception and illusion, able to manipulate both people and situations to their advantage.
